**Sikhae (식해) – A Traditional Korean Fermented Seafood Soup** Sikhae is a classic Korean dish that combines fresh seafood, vegetables, and a salty, slightly tangy fermented broth. It’s often served as a side dish (banchan) or a light main course, especially during the colder months when the warm, umami‑rich flavors are comforting. Below is a step‑by‑step guide to making a simple yet authentic sikhae at home. --- ## 1. What You’ll Need | Category | Typical Ingredients | Notes | |----------|---------------------|-------| | **Seafood** | • 200 g fresh white fish (e.g., cod, pollock, or halibut)
• 100 g shrimp or small prawns
• 50 g clams or mussels (optional) | Use the freshest seafood you can find. If you’re in a region where fresh fish isn’t available, frozen fish that has been thawed properly works fine. | | **Vegetables** | • 1 small carrot, julienned
• 1 small daikon radish, julienned
• 1 small zucchini, sliced
• 1 small onion, thinly sliced
• 1 small Korean pepper (gochu) or 1 tsp red pepper flakes (optional) | The vegetables add crunch and subtle sweetness. | | **Fermentation Base** | • 2 Tbsp Korean sea salt (or 1 Tbsp regular salt)
• 1 Tbsp Korean rice wine (makgeolli) or 1 Tbsp dry sherry (optional) | Salt is the key preservative; rice wine adds depth. | | **Broth** | • 4 cups water (or fish stock)
• 1 small piece of kombu (kelp) (optional)
• 1 small piece of dried anchovy (optional) | Kombu and anchovy give a subtle umami base. | | **Seasoning** | • 1 Tbsp Korean soybean paste (doenjang)
• 1 Tbsp Korean soybean sauce (ganjang)
• 1 tsp sugar (optional)
• 1 tsp sesame oil
• 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds
• 1 green onion, chopped
• 1 tsp minced garlic
• 1 tsp minced ginger | Adjust to taste. | | **Optional Add‑ons** | • 1 small Korean radish (mu) for extra crunch
• 1 small Korean pear (for sweetness)
• 1 small Korean cucumber (for freshness) | These are optional but add texture and flavor. | --- ## 2. Preparation Steps ### Step 1: Clean & Cut the Seafood 1. **Fish** – Remove skin and bones, then cut into bite‑size pieces. 2. **Shrimp** – Peel and devein. 3. **Clams/Mussels** – Rinse under cold water, discard any that open when tapped. ### Step 2: Salt the Seafood 1. Place all seafood in a bowl. 2. Sprinkle the sea salt evenly over the seafood. 3. Toss gently to coat. 4. Let it sit for **15–20 minutes**. This draws out moisture and starts the fermentation process. ### Step 3: Prepare the Vegetables 1. Wash and julienne carrots, daikon, zucchini, and onion. 2. If using Korean pepper, slice thinly. 3. Set aside. ### Step 4: Make the Fermented Broth 1. In a pot, combine water (or fish stock), kombu, and dried anchovy. 2. Bring to a gentle simmer for **5 minutes**. 3. Remove kombu and anchovy. 4. Stir in rice wine (if using). 5. Add the salted seafood and let it simmer for **10 minutes**. - *Tip:* Keep the heat low to avoid overcooking the seafood. ### Step 5: Add Vegetables & Seasonings 1. Add all prepared vegetables to the pot. 2. Stir in doenjang, ganjang, sugar (if using), minced garlic, and ginger. 3. Simmer for another **5–7 minutes** until vegetables are tender but still crisp. ### Step 6: Finish & Serve 1. Drizzle sesame oil over the soup. 2. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds, chopped green onions, and optional Korean pepper. 3. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed (more salt, more ganjang, or a splash of vinegar for acidity). 4. Ladle into bowls and serve hot. --- ## 3. Tips & Variations | Tip | Explanation | |-----|-------------| | **Use a small amount of salt** | Too much salt can overpower the delicate flavors. | | **Fermentation time** | If you prefer a stronger fermented taste, let the salted seafood sit for **30–45 minutes** before cooking. | | **Add a splash of vinegar** | A teaspoon of rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar brightens the broth. | | **Use different seafood** | Octopus, squid, or even crab can be substituted for variety. | | **Make it spicy** | Add more Korean pepper or a dash of gochujang for heat. | | **Serve with rice** | A bowl of steamed rice pairs wonderfully with sikhae. | | **Leftovers** | Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. The flavors deepen over time. | --- ## 4. Safety & Hygiene - **Freshness**: Always use fresh seafood. If you’re unsure, ask your fishmonger for the freshest catch. - **Salt**: Salt draws out moisture; ensure you don’t over‑salt. - **Cooking Temperature**: Keep the broth at a gentle simmer to preserve the texture of the seafood. - **Storage**: If you’re fermenting the seafood for longer than 24 hours, keep it refrigerated to prevent spoilage. --- ## 5. Quick Reference | Step | Action | Time | |------|--------|------| | 1 | Clean & cut seafood | 5 min | | 2 | Salt seafood | 15–20 min | | 3 | Prepare vegetables | 5 min | | 4 | Make broth & simmer seafood | 10 min | | 5 | Add veggies & seasonings | 5–7 min | | 6 | Finish & serve | 2 min | --- Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a comforting, umami‑rich dish that showcases the best of Korean seafood cuisine. Feel free to experiment with different seafood combinations and spice levels to suit your taste. Happy cooking!
